notice: SYNTHETIC EVALUATION FIXTURES. Every product, person, figure and quote below is invented for testing. None of it is market evidence and none of it may be cited as a source.
labelling: Labels were written from docs/evidence_rubric.md before any model was run on these cases, by the VentureLab developers with an AI coding assistant (Claude), which is not the model under test (Qwen3). Labels are not changed after seeing model output; the file's SHA-256 is recorded with every benchmark run.

cases.claim: At least one freelance translator reports spending hours each month checking which clients have paid.
cases.quote: Every month I spend around three hours working out which of my clients have actually paid.
cases.context: I'm a freelance translator. Every month I spend around three hours working out which of my clients have actually paid. It is the most boring part of the job.
cases.rationale: A first-person statement by a translator matches the claim's scope of at least one translator.

cases.claim: PodTrim's Basic plan costs $12 per month.
cases.quote: The Basic plan is $12 per month, billed monthly.
cases.context: PodTrim pricing. The Basic plan is $12 per month, billed monthly. The Pro plan adds team seats for $29 per month.
cases.rationale: The product's own pricing page states the exact price.

cases.claim: In the cited survey, 61% of the 412 responding tutors named rescheduling lessons as their biggest admin task.
cases.quote: Of the 412 tutors who responded, 61% named rescheduling lessons as their single biggest admin task.
cases.context: Survey method: an online questionnaire sent to members of a tutoring network. Of the 412 tutors who responded, 61% named rescheduling lessons as their single biggest admin task. Invoicing came second.
cases.rationale: The claim restates the survey result with the same scope.

cases.claim: The template seller refunded fewer than 2% of orders in 2025.
cases.quote: In 2025 I refunded 9 of 640 orders, about 1.4%.
cases.context: Year in review for my Notion template shop. In 2025 I refunded 9 of 640 orders, about 1.4%. Most refunds were duplicate purchases.
cases.rationale: 1.4% is below 2%, stated by the seller about their own shop.

cases.claim: At least one user in the thread asked for a way to export flashcards to CSV.
cases.quote: Is there any way to export my decks to CSV? I've asked support twice.
cases.context: Thread: Export options. Is there any way to export my decks to CSV? I've asked support twice. Reply: Not yet, it's on the roadmap.
cases.rationale: The user directly asks for CSV export of their flashcard decks.

cases.claim: Most small online shops struggle to write product descriptions.
cases.quote: Writing product descriptions for 300 items took me two full weeks.
cases.context: I run a small online shop selling printable planners. Writing product descriptions for 300 items took me two full weeks.
cases.rationale: One shop's experience cannot establish a claim about most shops.

cases.claim: Wedding planners will pay for a seating-chart app.
cases.quote: I'd love an app that does seating charts automatically, it would save me a day per wedding.
cases.context: As a wedding planner, the seating chart is always last-minute chaos. I'd love an app that does seating charts automatically, it would save me a day per wedding.
cases.rationale: Shows interest and a time cost for one planner, not willingness to pay.

cases.claim: Teachers in Germany and France use the resume builder.
cases.quote: Our users include teachers from Germany.
cases.context: Our users include teachers from Germany. We're working on a French version for next year.
cases.rationale: Germany is supported; France is not, since the French version does not exist yet.

cases.claim: The code-review bot reduced review time by 40% across all customer teams.
cases.quote: One customer team saw review time drop by 40% after adopting the bot.
cases.context: Case study. One customer team saw review time drop by 40% after adopting the bot. Results for other teams are still being collected.
cases.rationale: One team, not all teams.

cases.claim: Podcast hosts spend over five hours editing each episode and want to outsource it.
cases.quote: Editing eats up about six hours per episode for me.
cases.context: Editing eats up about six hours per episode for me. I'm not sure what else I'd do with the time.
cases.rationale: One host supports the time part; nothing supports wanting to outsource, and it is one host, not hosts in general.

cases.claim: Freelancers prefer subscription pricing over one-off purchases for invoicing tools.
cases.quote: I send invoice reminders manually every Friday.
cases.context: I send invoice reminders manually every Friday. It takes about twenty minutes.
cases.rationale: Describes a task, says nothing about pricing preferences.

cases.claim: The language app has more than 1 million downloads.
cases.quote: The app supports 14 languages and works offline.
cases.context: Features. The app supports 14 languages and works offline. Lessons take five minutes.
cases.rationale: Feature list, no download figures.

cases.claim: Remote teams regularly lose meeting notes.
cases.quote: Our team switched from Zoom to Google Meet last year.
cases.context: Our team switched from Zoom to Google Meet last year. The move took a week.
cases.rationale: About changing video tools, not about losing notes.

cases.claim: Etsy sellers find shipping labels hard to print.
cases.quote: I sell digital planners on Etsy, so there is nothing to ship.
cases.context: I sell digital planners on Etsy, so there is nothing to ship. My main problem is people sharing the files.
cases.rationale: This seller does not ship at all, so it says nothing about printing labels; it does not refute the claim either.

cases.claim: The onboarding redesign increased user retention.
cases.quote: We redesigned onboarding in March.
cases.context: We redesigned onboarding in March. We haven't analysed the retention numbers yet.
cases.rationale: The redesign happened but its effect is unknown.

cases.claim: Most survey respondents said they would pay for automated meeting summaries.
cases.quote: Only 12% of respondents said they would pay for automated meeting summaries; 71% said they would not.
cases.context: Results. Only 12% of respondents said they would pay for automated meeting summaries; 71% said they would not. The rest were unsure.
cases.rationale: 71% would not pay, the opposite of most would.

cases.claim: PodTrim offers a free plan.
cases.quote: PodTrim does not offer a free plan, only a 7-day trial.
cases.context: FAQ. PodTrim does not offer a free plan, only a 7-day trial.
cases.rationale: States there is no free plan.

cases.claim: The resume builder supports PDF export.
cases.quote: PDF export is not available yet; you can download Word files.
cases.context: Help centre. PDF export is not available yet; you can download Word files.
cases.rationale: PDF export is explicitly not available.

cases.claim: Sign-ups to the Excel course waitlist grew every month in 2025.
cases.quote: Waitlist sign-ups fell in four of the twelve months of 2025
cases.context: Course update. Waitlist sign-ups fell in four of the twelve months of 2025, mostly over the summer.
cases.rationale: Sign-ups fell in four months, so they did not grow every month.

cases.claim: Users in the thread say the flashcard app syncs reliably between devices.
cases.quote: Sync breaks constantly between my phone and laptop.
cases.context: Thread: Sync issues. Sync breaks constantly between my phone and laptop. Reply: Same here, I lost a week of reviews.
cases.rationale: Both users report unreliable sync.

cases.claim: Yoga studio owners struggle with class-booking software.
cases.quote: The new stadium will open in 2027 with 40,000 seats.
cases.context: City news. The new stadium will open in 2027 with 40,000 seats.
cases.rationale: Unrelated topic.

cases.claim: Freelance designers want a portfolio tool with client proofing.
cases.quote: Preheat the oven to 200 degrees and bake for 25 minutes.
cases.context: Recipe. Preheat the oven to 200 degrees and bake for 25 minutes.
cases.rationale: Unrelated topic.

cases.claim: Podcast listeners prefer episodes under 30 minutes.
cases.quote: Our cookie policy explains how we use analytics cookies.
cases.context: Footer. Our cookie policy explains how we use analytics cookies. All rights reserved.
cases.rationale: Website boilerplate.

cases.claim: Online tutors need tools for tracking homework.
cases.quote: Sign up for our newsletter to get 10% off your first order.
cases.context: Sign up for our newsletter to get 10% off your first order.
cases.rationale: Marketing boilerplate.

cases.claim: SaaS founders find churn analysis difficult.
cases.quote: The river flooded twice last spring, closing the bridge.
cases.context: Local report. The river flooded twice last spring, closing the bridge.
cases.rationale: Unrelated topic.

cases.claim: The reviewer recommends the template pack.
cases.quote: I would recommend this template pack
cases.context: I would recommend this template pack if half of it weren't broken. As it is, I asked for a refund.
cases.rationale: The recommendation is conditional and the reviewer asked for a refund.

cases.claim: The author believes AI writing tools will replace copywriters.
cases.quote: AI writing tools will replace copywriters
cases.context: People keep telling me that AI writing tools will replace copywriters. I think that's wrong; my bookings doubled this year.
cases.rationale: The author reports others' view and rejects it.

cases.claim: The study found that the app improved vocabulary scores.
cases.quote: the app improved vocabulary scores
cases.context: We hypothesised that the app improved vocabulary scores, but the results showed no significant difference between groups.
cases.rationale: It was a hypothesis that the results did not confirm.

cases.claim: The poster's team switched to TaskGrid.
cases.quote: We're switching to TaskGrid
cases.context: Our manager announced "We're switching to TaskGrid" in January, then cancelled the plan a week later after the trial.
cases.rationale: The switch was announced and then cancelled.

cases.claim: Freelancers lose clients because of late invoices.
cases.quote: Do freelancers lose clients because of late invoices?
cases.context: Do freelancers lose clients because of late invoices? That's the question I'm researching; I don't have data yet.
cases.rationale: A research question with no data, not a finding.

cases.claim: Demand for AI meeting summaries is growing among small agencies.
cases.quote: This article explains what AI meeting summaries are and how they work.
cases.context: This article explains what AI meeting summaries are and how they work. We cover transcription, speaker detection and summarisation.
cases.rationale: Explains the technology, says nothing about demand.

cases.claim: Online course creators struggle with video hosting costs.
cases.quote: In this guide we compare five video hosting platforms for online courses.
cases.context: In this guide we compare five video hosting platforms for online courses. Each section lists features and supported formats.
cases.rationale: A comparison guide, no evidence of creators struggling with cost.

cases.claim: Remote workers want better focus-timer apps.
cases.quote: Focus timer apps have been around since the Pomodoro technique became popular.
cases.context: History corner. Focus timer apps have been around since the Pomodoro technique became popular.
cases.rationale: History of the category, not what remote workers want.

cases.claim: Indie authors lose sales because of poor book-cover design.
cases.quote: Book cover design is one of the topics covered in our self-publishing course
cases.context: Course outline. Book cover design is one of the topics covered in our self-publishing course, alongside formatting and pricing.
cases.rationale: Lists a course topic, no evidence about lost sales.

cases.claim: Small nonprofits cannot afford donor-management software.
cases.quote: Donor-management software is used by nonprofits to track gifts and contacts.
cases.context: Glossary. Donor-management software is used by nonprofits to track gifts and contacts.
cases.rationale: A definition, nothing about affordability.

cases.claim: There is demand among freelancers for an automated invoice-matching tool.
cases.quote: PayMatch is an app that matches bank payments to invoices.
cases.context: PayMatch is an app that matches bank payments to invoices. It connects to most European banks.
cases.rationale: A product existing does not show demand.

cases.claim: Freelancers are willing to pay for invoice-matching software.
cases.quote: PayMatch says it has 8,000 paying subscribers, mostly freelancers.
cases.context: Company profile. PayMatch says it has 8,000 paying subscribers, mostly freelancers.
cases.rationale: People paying a competitor is indirect evidence, and the figure is self-reported.

cases.claim: PayMatch charges 9 euros per month after its trial.
cases.quote: PayMatch costs 9 euros per month after a 14-day trial.
cases.context: Pricing. PayMatch costs 9 euros per month after a 14-day trial.
cases.rationale: A claim about the competitor itself, stated on its pricing page.

cases.claim: Podcast hosts want an AI editing tool.
cases.quote: There are at least six AI podcast editing tools on the market, including PodTrim and CutCast.
cases.context: Market overview. There are at least six AI podcast editing tools on the market, including PodTrim and CutCast.
cases.rationale: Supply of tools is not evidence of what hosts want.

cases.claim: Small agencies will pay for client-reporting dashboards.
cases.quote: AgencyView raised $4 million to build client-reporting dashboards.
cases.context: Funding news. AgencyView raised $4 million to build client-reporting dashboards.
cases.rationale: Investor funding is not customer demand.
